Day 1: define the business decision, target, costs, and success metric; inspect schema, missingness, duplicates, timestamps, and label availability. Create a leak-free temporal/entity split, then compare a dumb heuristic with a fast linear/GBDT or pretrained baseline. By 5 PM, deliver reproducible code, held-out metrics, representative errors, and known limitations. [1](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/guides/rules-of-ml)

Week 1: audit labels and worst errors, fix data/split issues, establish versioned datasets and a reproducible pipeline. Week 2: iterate on the highest-value data/features, build serving with input/schema checks, monitoring, load tests, and rollback. Week 3: shadow, canary, evaluate guardrails, document ownership, and expand only if criteria pass. [2](https://research.google/pubs/the-ml-test-score-a-rubric-for-ml-production-readiness-and-technical-debt-reduction/) [3](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/)

Three weeks is a planning target, not a universal promise: missing labels, integrations, validation requirements, or poor baseline quality can change scope. Agree on a narrow supported release and make unresolved risks visible through explicit launch criteria.
